correctness.rationale: The proof independently establishes full factor coverage at each triadic length from the lack of adjacent nonzero substitution blocks; every padded prefix and suffix occurs in the image of factor 010. Palindromic W_k gives two candidate classes at each positive weight; ternary position decoding yields even internal gaps 3^{nu_2(i)}+1 and a unique odd circular wrap gap. Conjugacy under reversal is therefore equivalent to an internal valuation-palindrome; its unique maximum forces j a power of two, and powers of two satisfy the converse. All k>=0 and j boundaries are covered; the independent base-three and morphism-based Python checker found 2,3,6,13,28,59,122,249 classes for k=0..7 with exact tested factor sets.

Lü et al., DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2015.12.022, report ordinary factor count 2n-1 for the Cantor word and permutation complexity; these quantities do not specify cyclic conjugacy mergers.
Bell and Shallit, arXiv:2102.03821, count only conjugacy classes whose *every* rotation appears, a strictly different condition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither a general inequality between complexity measures nor formulas for a different measure/word give the exact Cantor rotation classes. The current proof identifies a marked odd gap and a power-of-two symmetry criterion not supplied by those prior statements.

value.rationale: The standard Cantor word provides a natural non-uniformly recurrent test case for cyclic complexity. The claim classifies every triadic-length necklace by weight for infinitely many lengths, explains the exact symmetry exceptions using binary valuations, and gives sublinear cyclic growth of order N^{log_3 2} along triadic lengths in contrast with the known linear ordinary factor complexity. The structural mechanism and exact invariant are mathematically motivated beyond numerical table generation.
